trust_decision.summary: Decided in Praxis (not in pingora): every downstream HTTP/2 session served by the proxy must be built with bounded H2Options (decoded header-list size and concurrent streams), and the fix supplies them at the single HttpProxy construction that serves both h2c prior-knowledge and TLS-ALPN h2 listeners.

landing_point.why: It is the only place an HttpProxy is constructed; an engineer reading 'HTTP/2 bomb' looks for where HTTP/2 server options are configured and finds h2c enabled here with no header-list or stream bounds.

fix_sites.entry_point: load_http_handler (public API), invoked once per `protocol: http` listener from PingoraHttp::register and used by both cleartext (h2c) and TLS (ALPN h2) listeners
fix_sites.module_kind: pingora HTTP reverse-proxy service wiring (private helper, not a route or handler hook)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None available: every HTTP/2-capable listener is served by the one HttpProxy built in wire_service, and the only other HTTP servers (admin and KV ServeHttp apps) bind plain TCP without enabling h2c, so no route can be argued out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: HTTP/2 itself must keep working on both transports: the conformance suite drives h2c prior-knowledge requests and TLS ALPN h2 requests, and the project's own health probe performs an h2c preface handshake, so a fix that disables h2c or drops h2 from listener ALPN breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: one HEADERS(+CONTINUATION) block whose HPACK-decoded header list is far larger than the compressed wire bytes (header-list amplification)
a single connection opening many concurrent request streams (stream-count amplification)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The admin ServeHttp app could enable h2c/h2 on the admin port (e.g. for gRPC-style health or metrics scraping) without ever setting h2_options, creating a second unbounded HTTP/2 server.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a separate server implementation (HttpServerApp/ServeHttp) in a different module from the proxy; a maintainer who wants HTTP/2 on /metrics or /ready would set HttpServerOptions.h2c and would have to know, separately, that h2 limits live on the other trait method.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The deprecated KV admin service is a second ServeHttp app with its own Service::new/add_tcp wiring where HTTP/2 could be turned on without h2 limits.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same shape as the admin service and is still a public registration function, so a maintainer extending admin transports would plausibly touch it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A load_http_handler_no_body loader for the already-exported PingoraHttpHandlerNoBody would build a second HttpProxy via http_proxy(), where the same H2Options assignment would be needed.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler type is public and exported but has no public loader today, so adding the no-body wiring path is a natural maintainer change and would silently miss the h2 settings.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Enabling HTTP/2 toward upstreams (peer.options.set_http_version) would make the proxy an h2 client whose HPACK decoder also needs a bounded header list, via a different API than the server-side H2Options.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Upstream HTTP/2 is a standard proxy feature and the peer is built in its own module from cluster config; a maintainer adding it would reuse HttpPeer::new here and not the downstream h2 options factory.

O9_family: CWE-409 improper handling of highly compressed data — HPACK header-list amplification and stream-count amplification against the HTTP/2 server, leading to memory exhaustion

O10_build.toolchain: cargo with rust-toolchain.toml pinning 1.96.0; pingora is consumed as the renamed fork crates quixotic-plecostomus-core/-http/-proxy 0.8.2 from crates.io
O10_build.project_tests: cargo test -p praxis-proxy-protocol for the handler unit tests; HTTP/2 behaviour is covered by tests/conformance/tests/suite/rfcs/rfc9113.rs (h2c via the h2 crate), tests/conformance/tests/suite/tls.rs:106 (ALPN h2) and tests/conformance/tests/suite/h2spec.rs (needs the external h2spec 2.6.0 binary that `make tools` downloads)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set h2c = false (or drop h2 from the listener ALPN list) so prior-knowledge HTTP/2 is unreachable, instead of bounding the decoded header list and stream count.
